Paper: Sendrier, On the Dimension of the Hull, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 10(2):282-293 (1997)
Main theorem: Number of distinct q-ary linear codes with a hull of a given dimension; asymptotic constant proportion
Difference from proposed work: Counts ALL linear codes, not constacyclic; no generator-polynomial structure, so it does not give the factor-orbit decomposition the proposed enumerator uses

Paper: Assmus & Key, Affine and projective planes, Discrete Math. 83 (1990)
Main theorem: Introduces the hull for the classification of finite projective planes
Difference from proposed work: Origin of the hull concept; no enumeration

Paper: Skersys, The average dimension of the hull of cyclic codes, Discrete Appl. Math. 128(1):275-292 (2003)
Main theorem: First expression for the AVERAGE hull dimension of cyclic codes
Difference from proposed work: Average only; the proposed work asks for the full distribution as a polynomial

Paper: Sangwisut, Jitman, Ling, Udomkavanich, Hulls of cyclic and negacyclic codes over finite fields, Finite Fields Appl. 33:232-257 (2015)
Main theorem: Generator-polynomial formula for the hull dimension and the NUMBER of codes with a given hull dimension
Difference from proposed work: Over a FIELD and for cyclic/negacyclic only; the proposed work is over the non-chain ring R_e and for lambda-constacyclic constituents

Paper: Jitman & Sangwisut, The average dimension of the Hermitian hull of cyclic codes over finite fields of square order, AIP Conf. Proc. 1775:030026 (2016)
Main theorem: Average Hermitian hull dimension
Difference from proposed work: Average, not distribution; cyclic only

Paper: Jitman & Sangwisut, The average dimension of the Hermitian hull of constacyclic codes over finite fields of square order, Adv. Math. Commun. 12(3):451-463 (2018), doi 10.3934/amc.2018027
Main theorem: Average Hermitian hull dimension of constacyclic codes plus upper/lower bounds; either 0 or grows at rate n
Difference from proposed work: CLOSEST field-level work on the SAME object (Hermitian hull of constacyclic over F_{q^2}) but gives only the mean; the proposed distribution would sharpen it from a moment to a law - and must be compared with the counting papers below before any novelty is claimed

Paper: Jitman, Sangwisut, Udomkavanich, Hulls of cyclic codes over Z_4, Discrete Math. 343(1):111621, doi 10.1016/j.disc.2019.111621 (2020)
Main theorem: Hull types and average 2-dimension E(n) = 5n/9 - 2B_n/9
Difference from proposed work: Chain ring, cyclic, average only

Paper: Jitman & Sangwisut, Hulls of cyclic codes over the ring F_2+vF_2, Thai J. Math. (2020)
Main theorem: Hull structure over a non-chain ring
Difference from proposed work: Non-chain ring but cyclic only and no hull-dimension count

Paper: Debnath & Prakash, Galois hulls of constacyclic codes over finite fields, Cryptogr. Commun., doi 10.1007/s12095-022-00591-6 (2022/2023)
Hull type: k-Galois (includes Euclidean k=0 and Hermitian k=m/2)
Main theorem: Formula for the Galois hull dimension via a suitable arrangement of the irreducible factors of x^n - lambda; THE NUMBER OF CONSTACCLIC CODES OF LENGTH n WITH A GIVEN GALOIS HULL DIMENSION is calculated
Exact enumeration?: YES - counts constacyclic codes by Galois hull dimension
Difference from proposed work: THE MOST DIRECT PRIOR ART for the proposed constituent enumerator H_l(z): a field-level exact count of constacyclic codes by Galois hull dimension already exists; Hermitian over F_{q^2} is the special case m=2, k=1

Paper: Debnath & Prakash, Average dimensions of Galois hulls of constacyclic codes, Adv. Math. Commun. 19(6):1569-1604 (2025), doi 10.3934/amc.2025010
Main theorem: Formula for the AVERAGE Galois hull dimension
Difference from proposed work: Average only; same authors as the counting paper, so the field-level counting programme is already theirs

Paper: Debnath & Prakash, Hulls of Cyclic Codes Over a Local Ring, ICTIS 2025, SIST vol. 325, pp. 309-319, doi 10.1007/978-981-95-1365-9_25 (online 25 Nov 2025)
Main theorem: Hull generators and types, a condition for LCD, an expression for the p-dimension, and A COUNT OF ALL CYCLIC CODES FOR A FIXED p-DIMENSION OF THE HULL
Exact enumeration?: YES - ring-level count by hull dimension
Difference from proposed work: Ring-level exact counting already exists for a CHAIN ring; the proposed work targets the non-chain R_e with e components - the gap, if any, is narrower than 'no ring-level counts exist'

Paper: Debnath, Islam, Martinez-Moro, Prakash, Galois hulls of constacyclic codes over affine algebra rings, Discrete Math. 349(2):114750 (2026); arXiv:2412.08512
Main theorem: Galois hull dimension over an affine algebra ring; cardinality of the set of q-dimensions of k-Galois hulls
Exact enumeration?: partial - counts the SET of dimensions, delta_k(n,q,lambda), not the number of codes per dimension
Difference from proposed work: Present in this workspace as the rejected non-source PDF; nearest ring-level relative; it counts the SET of attainable dimensions, not a distribution over codes

Paper: Lu, Yang, Liu, Fu, Guo, Hermitian Hulls of Cyclic Codes and Exact Dual Distances of Extended Linear Codes, arXiv:2607.12242 (v1 Jul 2026, v3 Oct 2026)
Main theorem: Structure theory of the Hermitian hull via defining sets; r additive over tau-orbits with a parity constraint; a PRODUCT ENUMERATOR in Appendix B ('Counting and the fine structure of the tau-fixed cosets') supplying the exact counts, the scarcity probability, and the mean and variance
Exact enumeration?: YES - exact counts of cyclic codes by hull codimension (a product enumerator, Appendix B)
Difference from proposed work: An exact enumerator by hull dimension for a Hermitian hull already exists, for CYCLIC codes, as of October 2026; any claim that 'the enumerator is new' must be restricted to the constacyclic-over-R_e object. The same paper states that codes had already been enumerated by hull dimension for cyclic and negacyclic codes (Sangwisut et al., Thms 22 and 23)

Paper: Enumeration and Monotonicity of Linear Codes with Prescribed Hull Dimensions, arXiv:2605.29204 (2026)
Main theorem: A^H_{n,k,l,q^2} = number of [n,k] codes over F_{q^2} with Hermitian hull dimension l; monotonicity
Exact enumeration?: YES - counts by Hermitian hull dimension
Difference from proposed work: Counts all linear codes; no cyclic/constacyclic structure

Paper: Shi, Huang, Yue, Construction of new quantum codes derived from constacyclic codes over F_{q^2}+uF_{q^2}+...+u^{r-1}F_{q^2}, Appl. Algebra Engrg. Comm. Comput. 32(5):603-620 (2021)
Main theorem: Quantum codes from constacyclic codes over the SAME ring family the source paper uses
Difference from proposed work: Same ring family and same quantum target, but no hull-dimension distribution and no enumeration by hull dimension

Paper: Islam, Prakash, Verma, New quantum codes from constacyclic codes over the ring R_{k,m}, Adv. Math. Commun. 16(1):17-35 (2022)
Main theorem: Quantum codes from constacyclic codes over a non-chain ring
Difference from proposed work: Quantum construction only; no enumeration

Paper: Hulls of constacyclic codes over finite non-chain rings and their applications in quantum codes construction, Quantum Inf. Process., doi 10.1007/s11128-023-04230-8 (2023)
Main theorem: Dimensions of hulls of Gray images of constacyclic codes over a non-chain ring; quantum codes via construction X
Difference from proposed work: Same theme (hull dimensions of Gray images over a non-chain ring) but no code counts and no joint/component structure

Paper: Yadav, Singh, Islam, Prakash, Sole, Hermitian hull of constacyclic codes over a class of non-chain rings and new quantum codes, Comput. Appl. Math. 43:269 (2024) - THE SOURCE
Main theorem: Possible Hermitian hull dimensions (Thm 8, Thm 10); Hermitian LCD criterion (Thm 11/13, Cor 12/14); dual-containing criterion (Thm 15/16); Gray map + quantum codes
Exact enumeration?: NO - gives the SET of possible dimensions and bounds, never a count of codes
Difference from proposed work: The source gives the admissible set of hull dimensions over R_e; the proposed project proposes to count codes by hull dimension. That step is new ONLY IF the field-level counts do not compose trivially over the e components

Paper: Dinh, On the linear ordering of some classes of negacyclic and cyclic codes and their distance distributions, Finite Fields Appl. 14(1):22-40 (2008); formula restated as Lemma 1 of arXiv:2304.00762 and Thm 2.4 of arXiv:1704.03311
Main theorem: EXACT minimum distance d_i=(tau+1)p^t for every i on p^s-p^{s-t}+(tau-1)p^{s-t-1} < i <= p^s-p^{s-t}+tau p^{s-t-1}
Exact enumeration?: YES - exact distance for every i, every p, every s
Difference from proposed work: Settles the entire distance side of the single-orbit repeated-root family; the P3-7 conjecture IS this theorem and the P3-7 tables reproduce it (5050 values verified). No hull content, so R4 is unaffected

Paper: Debnath & Prakash, Hulls of Cyclic Codes Over a Local Ring, ICTIS 2025, Smart Innovation Systems and Technologies 325:309-319, DOI 10.1007/978-981-95-1365-9_25
Main theorem: Generator forms and characterisation of hulls; LCD condition; hull types; expression for the p-dimensions of the hulls; for a fixed hull p-dimension, counts ALL cyclic codes
Exact enumeration?: YES - count of codes by hull p-dimension (abstract; body paywalled)
Difference from proposed work: MARGINAL law on hull dimension over a fixed chain ring, no Gray map and no distance. Does not give a joint (hull,d) law, which is what R4 needs; absence not established since the body is unread

Paper: Debnath, Prakash & Islam, Correction to: Galois hulls of constacyclic codes over finite fields, Cryptogr. Commun. 15:129-130 (2023), DOI 10.1007/s12095-022-00602-6
Main theorem: Correction to the 2023 paper; per its summary it clarifies that a primitive element of F_8 is needed for the definition of constacyclic codes used there
Difference from proposed work: Bibliographic: means blocker B-2a is TWO unread documents, not one. Any appeal to the 2023 paper must be read against the corrected text
